# Zhex

> Zhex is a Forth-inspired programming language built on small words and big ideas: compact code with visible flow, meaningful names, and checked types, executed by a working Go interpreter. Every program is checked — names, types, and word connections — before any of it runs.

## Docs

- [Manifesto](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/manifesto.html): the intentions behind Zhex — visible data, small composed words, a language machines can read, errors that teach, performance you can measure, and code humans enjoy reviewing. Full text at docs/manifesto.md; concrete goals at docs/language-goals.md.
- [Docs](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs.html): a grouped guide to getting started, language concepts, the standard library, and tools, with separate topic pages.
- [Getting started](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/getting-started.html): install and run a first program.
- [Language](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/syntax.html): syntax, values, words, flows, control flow, Results, and modules.
- [Records and named types](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/records.html): nominal record declarations, positional construction, immutable fields, and explicit type annotations.
- [Choices and matching](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/choices.html): concrete named alternatives, payload binding, exhaustive cases, and a final `case _` default.
- [Lists and arrays](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/collections.html): homogeneous shared collections, checked indexing, resizing, limits, and failure handling.
- [Maps](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/maps.html): typed inferred keys and values, `Option` lookup, insertion-ordered iteration, updates, and flows.
- [JSON](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/json.html): typed JSON decoding with record defaults, strict validation and field paths, and encoding of supported values.
- [Collection iteration](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/iteration.html): list indices, array coordinates, row-major arrays, insertion-ordered map traversal, and mutation guards.
- Rich-value rules: record declarations and choices are nominal. Record constructors take fields in order and may omit trailing field defaults; defaults evaluate freshly in declaration scope. `type Names = alias List<String>` defines a transparent alias. Fields are immutable; choice alternatives are constructed by qualified name, with payloads in declared order. A choice may have one type parameter: payload constructors infer it, while a nullary alternative needs an expected type. Generic records and words are not supported. Match every alternative once, or use one final `case _`; a default after all named alternatives is an error. Choices cannot be printed or compared directly, payloads cannot contain `Result`, and caught concrete errors need `error.wrap` before storing in an `Error` payload. Lists infer homogeneous elements; empty list values need an expected `List<T>`. Arrays use explicit `List<Int>` shapes, rank 2..32, and at most 1,000,000 elements. List/array reads, `array.new`, `list.append`, and `array.resize` return ordinary values and diagnose invalid operations at runtime; direct `try` or `catch` selects a checked Result for that operation only. Plain indexed writes return `Unit` and raise runtime diagnostics for invalid rank, bounds, or active-iteration mutation; parenthesized indexed writes return a checked `Result<Unit, Error>`. `Map<K, V>` infers types from nonempty literals; empty maps need an expected type. Map literal keys are constant `String`, `Int`, or `Bool` literals; dynamic keys are allowed for lookup, update, containment, and removal. Lookup yields `Option<V>` without `try`, and map values cannot contain `Result`. Map iteration preserves insertion order. Mutation of an actively traversed map raises a runtime `collection-iterating` diagnostic before changing storage; it is not a `Result`. Collection aliases share storage. Caught concrete errors may go directly to built-in `error.*` operations, but require `error.wrap` before passing to a user word expecting `Error` or storing in an Error-typed record field or collection; flow cannot pass Error values to user-defined steps.
- [Standard library](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/text.html): text, buffers, files, and console operations.
- JSON: `json.decode(raw, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`; missing record fields use defaults, invalid supplied fields do not. Present Lists/Maps replace defaults, and each decoded value gets fresh copies of mutable defaults while aliases inside that value remain shared. `json.encode(value)` returns compact JSON; record fields follow declaration order and Map keys follow insertion order. Supported types are `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, and `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`; `null` means `Option.None`. Int accepts signed 64-bit integer-form JSON tokens only; decimal/exponent notation and overflow reject. Arrays, resources, Results, non-Option choices, and non-string-key maps are unsupported. JSON errors include `json-syntax`, `json-type`, `json-field`, `json-range`, and `json-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, with root as empty string and `~`/`/` escaped as `~0`/`~1`.
- [Tools](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/repl.html): the REPL, diagnostics, and editor support.
- Vocabulary: text work uses the `text.*` words — `length` (code points), `line-count`, `word-count`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `contains`, `index-of` (code-point position, `-1` when absent), `slice(start, end)` (code points, bounds clamp, `start >= end` is empty), `replace(old, new)` (every occurrence, literal, empty `old` errors), plus the earlier `reverse` and `to-int`. Lines build in a `Buffer`: `buffer.new()`, `buffer.add-line`, `buffer.line-count`, `buffer.line(i)` and `buffer.set-line(i, text)` (Results failing `buffer-range` on a bad index), `buffer.to-text`; `let` binds the buffer's name — two names observe one buffer — and `Buffer` is excluded from `==` and rejected by `print` (convert with `buffer.to-text`). Files read whole (`file.read-all(path)` to String, `file.read-lines(path)` to a Buffer of chomped lines) or streamed (`file.open(path)`, `file.read-line(f)` where end of file fails inside the Result, `file.close(f)` idempotent); `for line in file.lines(path)` streams chomped lines and guarantees the close on every exit, including loop-body failures. File Results fail `file-open`, `file-read`, or `file-utf8`, naming the path and the operating system's reason. Program arguments forward as `zhex run file.zhex [args...]`: read them with `console.args-count()` and `console.arg(i)` (a Result failing `argument-missing` on a bad index).
- Results and errors: built-ins return explicit `Result<T, E>`. User words declare success types; an escaping `try` infers one error family and an effective Result signature, and successful values are wrapped once. Pure words keep their declared type. Explicit `Result<T, E>` signatures remain supported with `ok`/`err`, without wrapping twice. Each caller still uses `try` or `catch`; multiple uncaught families in one word are rejected, so catch a failure or explicitly wrap it as common `Error`. Runtime faults are not inferred. `catch [name]` lazily supplies a same-typed fallback or exits via `console.exit`/`console.fail`. Bare Results cannot be discarded; a stored `let pending = call()` must be handled by the immediately following same-block statement as exactly `pending try` or `pending catch ...`, standalone or as a whole new `let` RHS. Explicit flow steps use `word-name try`. `error.new` creates a cause-less application Error; `error.wrap` converts to common `Error` and preserves the cause; accessors include code/message/operation/file/line/column/detail/has-cause/cause. File detail `reason` values are `not-found`, `permission-denied`, `other` (open), and `invalid-utf8`, `closed`, `read-failed`, `end-of-file` (read). `error.set-reporter(named-word)` installs a top-level `(Error) -> Unit` callback. `error.report(problem)` reports a handled occurrence; a failure escaping the program calls the reporter once before the diagnostic. Intermediate propagation does not report, duplicate occurrences are suppressed, callback failure/recursion is isolated, and no external destination is configured by default. `console.exit(status)` ends execution with 0..255, and `console.fail(message)` writes to stderr and ends with status 1; neither reports a valid deliberate exit. Out-of-range exit status is a runtime diagnostic. These exits close active `file.lines` streams; explicitly opened files still require `file.close`. Reporter calls to either operation cannot replace the original outcome.
- Modules: split a program across files with `use math` — it loads the sibling `math.zhex` next to the importing file (each file's own imports resolve beside it; the REPL resolves against the working directory and adopts the module for the session). Imported words are called qualified (`math.gcd(a, b)`); module words call each other bare inside their own file and cannot see the importer's words; a module's own imports stay private to it, and two modules never collide. A leading underscore makes a word or type module-private: calling one from outside fails `private-use`, and it is never suggested cross-module. A public signature, record field, or choice payload cannot expose a private type, even through a List, Array, Map, or Result. Imported choice constructors and cases are qualified (`model.Status.Ready`). Errors: a missing module fails `use-missing` naming the searched path; import cycles fail `use-cycle` spelling the files; module names `text`, `int`, `buffer`, `file`, `console`, `error`, `list`, `array`, `map`, and `json` fail `use-reserved`; the built-in `Option` type and constructors are reserved names, but `Option` is not a reserved module name. Imported files may declare words and types but top-level statements fail `module-body`; `use` outside a file's top level fails `use-location` — and `use` is a reserved word. Loaded modules check before their importers, and module errors annotate the module's own source. Trace events carry qualified names (`{"word":"math.gcd"}`, module-private words included) with word returns pointing into the module file (`{"file":"math.zhex"}`). Corpus example: `examples/modules/main.zhex`, a two-file program run as `zhex run examples/modules/main.zhex`.
- [Examples](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples.html): runnable programs with source, sample input, and real output — the source and output on the page are produced by the actual interpreter. `text-stats` is the first real application: run it as `zhex run examples/text-stats.zhex <file> [upper]` — one argument reports the file's line, word, and character counts from one whole read, and any second argument streams the file uppercased line by line.
- [Roadmap](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/roadmap.html): what is done, what is next, and what is future, mirrored by a public project board.
- [Error catalog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html): built-in diagnostic codes with their meanings and fixes; application codes from `error.new`/`error.wrap` are not catalog entries. Diagnostics print `file:line:column: message` plus an excerpt, caret, and `hint:` line; `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` emits the machine-readable report `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}`, plus optional additive span_start_column/span_end_column (checker diagnostics with a span, never runtime).
- [Development insight](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/diagnostics-plan.md): `zhex run file.zhex --trace` streams JSONL step events to stderr — one JSON object per line, emitted before any diagnostic, and combinable with `--report=json` (events, then the report). Four events: `{"event":"word-call","word":W,"file":F,"line":N,"args":[...]}`, `{"event":"binding","name":N,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"flow-step","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"word-return","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`. `word-call` fires only for program words — builtins never emit it; they appear as flow-step or binding effects. Bindings holding a `Result` (a read without postfix `try`) render `ok("inner")` or `err("message")`; other values render per the checker's static types — Int as digits, Bool as `true`/`false`, String verbatim, Unit as the empty string, Buffer as `buffer(<n> lines)`, File as `file("<path>")` — and a `-> Unit` word returns value "". Tracing never fails a run, and output without the flag is unchanged.
- REPL: `zhex repl [--trace]` runs an interactive session where words and values persist across entries; agents can script a session by piping entries to the command's standard input. A blank line ends a multi-line entry — only a missing indented block continues, so statements never span lines. Bare ordinary expressions echo their value; naked Result expressions are rejected and must be handled with `try` or `catch` in the same entry. `words` lists effective signatures sorted by name (including inferred Result effects and shadows a user binding of that name); a word can be redefined with the same effective signature, while an incompatible signature change is rejected transactionally. `let` shadows silently. Check and runtime errors print the annotated diagnostic and the session survives; a runtime error keeps the entry's earlier effects. A final input line without a trailing newline still runs, and Ctrl-D exits 0. With `--trace`, the same JSONL step events as `zhex run` stream to stderr with `"file":"repl"`.

## Reference

- [Language contract](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/initial-language.md): the authoritative syntax and semantics the interpreter enforces.
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for writing correct Zhex and verifying changes with the executable test suite.
- [Example sources](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples/hello.zhex): downloadable `.zhex` files — swap the filename for fizzbuzz, fibonacci, gcd, times-table, factorial, palindrome, composition, records, choices, collections, maps, json-config, text-stats, recovery, or exit-status; the two-file modules program lives at examples/modules/main.zhex with its math.zhex beside it.
- [Project board](https://github.com/users/desireco/projects/8): the backlog and delivered work as issues on a public Kanban board.
